clips.title: The story
paras: Nikova Raskol grieves for Mac, her young grandson, killed inside Stormwind City's prison. Anger consumes her, and she sends adventurers into The Stockade to take the Defias gang's red bandanas in retribution.

Mac Raskol was fourteen when he took up arms as a guard in The Stockade. Stormwind's regular soldiers had been sent to distant fronts, leaving local defense to volunteers and the city's youth. Mac watched hardened criminals and mutinous members of the Defias Brotherhood in a place far more dangerous than his experience could prepare him for.

The Defias inmates tore apart their wool prison blankets and made red bandanas from the scraps. The colors marked their loyalty to the Brotherhood, even behind prison walls. When Mac rebuked them and tried to enforce discipline, the prisoners stabbed him in the back. He died on the stone floor.

Nikova Raskol turns from official channels to cold revenge after Mac's pointless death. She sends you into The Stockade to quell the rioting prisoners and bring back ten of their cherished red bandanas. Dyed the color of her grandson's spilled blood, the tokens offer a broken family a grim sense of closure.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: Bitterness flows through my veins like a cold river. My grandson, Mac, was such a good boy. A mere 14 years old. When the army was sent off to the front, Mac took up arms to defend the city. He was a guard in The Stockade, where the Defias gang is locked up. Mac reprimanded some of the prisoners for tearing their wool blankets to make scarves, a symbol of their gang. For that Mac was stabbed in the back.
I want revenge. Bring me 10 of their precious Wool Bandanas. They are the color of blood.

clips.title: Progress
paras: I see you are back, adventurer. Have you collected 10 Red Wool Bandanas from those Defias Scum in The Stockade yet?

clips.title: Completion
paras: So these bandanas -- filthy tokens of corruption -- are what my Mac had to die for? Such a waste. Such a tragic sacrifice.
But alas, I cannot return to the past. Just know, friend, that you have brought my family justice through your deeds.
